Tishri
TISH-ree
proper noun
The post-exilic name of the seventh month of the sacred year, from the Babylonian Tashrītu, “beginning”; the same as the older Ethanim, the great festal month.

📖 Biblical Definition

Tishri is the later name of the seventh month of the sacred year, the month older called Ethanim, answering to the close of September and beginning of October. Though the name Tishri itself is not written in the Scriptures, the month it names is the crown of the sacred calendar, for in it fall the three great appointments of the seventh month: the feast of trumpets on the first day, “a memorial of blowing of trumpets, an holy convocation” (Lev 23:24); the day of atonement on the tenth, when the people afflicted their souls and the high priest went in before the mercy seat (Lev 23:27); and the feast of tabernacles from the fifteenth, when Israel dwelt in booths and rejoiced before the LORD (Lev 23:34). In this month too Ezra read the law before the congregation on the first day (Neh 8:2). So the seventh month is a gospel in miniature: the trumpet summons, the blood atones, and the people rejoice in the ingathered harvest and the tabernacling presence of God. Let the believer hear in the trumpet the call to worship, see in the day of atonement the blood of Christ that alone can put away sin, and taste in the feast of tabernacles the joy of God dwelling with His people, which shall be full and endless in the world to come.

📜 Webster 1828 Definition

The post-exilic name of the seventh month of the sacred year, the same as Ethanim; the great festal month of trumpets, atonement, and tabernacles.

TISHRI, the seventh month of the sacred year among the Hebrews, the same as the older Ethanim.

The name is of Babylonian origin, and is not itself written in the Scriptures.

It answers to the close of September and beginning of October.

In it fall the feast of trumpets, the day of atonement, and the feast of tabernacles.

It is the crown of the sacred calendar, rich in holy convocations.

📖 Key Scripture

Lev 23:24 — "Speak unto the children of Israel, saying, In the seventh month, in the first day of the month, shall ye have a sabbath, a memorial of blowing of trumpets, an holy convocation."

Lev 23:27 — "Also on the tenth day of this seventh month there shall be a day of atonement: it shall be an holy convocation unto you; and ye shall afflict your souls, and offer an offering made by fire unto the LORD."

Lev 23:34 — "Speak unto the children of Israel, saying, The fifteenth day of this seventh month shall be the feast of tabernacles for seven days unto the LORD."

Neh 8:2 — "And Ezra the priest brought the law before the congregation both of men and women, and all that could hear with understanding, upon the first day of the seventh month."

⚠️ Modern Corruption

A festal month of Scripture, not a contested doctrine; the seventh month is a gospel in miniature — the trumpet summons, the blood atones, the people rejoice in God’s presence.

expand to see more

Tishri faces no postmodern redefinition. The truth it carries answers the modern hollowing of the holy days into mere custom or festival, stripped of the gospel they preach — the trumpet, the blood, and the booth emptied of their meaning and kept, if at all, as sentiment.

This entry faces no significant postmodern redefinition. The principle to recover is that the seventh month preaches Christ. The trumpet summons the people to worship; the day of atonement points to the blood that alone puts away sin; the feast of tabernacles foretastes the joy of God dwelling with His people. The believer hears the trumpet as a call to worship, rests in the atoning blood of Christ, and looks for the day when the tabernacle of God shall be with men for ever.
